sermon.title: Helps
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the ministry of helps: the wise men financing Jesus’ flight to Egypt, deacons qualified by honest report, the Spirit and wisdom, the church’s welfare policy in 1 Timothy 5 and 2 Thessalonians 3, the four men carrying the paralytic, the apostles serving the multitude, and thrifty ministers. Help begins at home; good families make a good church.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Several phrases not clear. Points to check: “7,000 saved at two different times” (Acts 2:41 and 4:4 give 3,000 and 5,000); 15,000 at the feeding; wise men travelling two years; angels without wings; his citing 1 Corinthians 9:14 for preaching without charge (9:18); “over fifty percent chance” of ending up alone; leading almost 1,100 people to Christ (personal). Sensitive content kept as spoken: the New Testament church never helping unbelievers, the woman as manager/“head” of the house, marriage for sexual desire, prosperity preachers, homosexuals.

chunks.section_question: Where does the ministry of helps fit among the gifts?
chunks.short_answer: God sets people in the church—Bible college or Ivy League schools can’t. He ranks the utterance ministries (apostle, prophet, teacher), then sign ministries (miracles, healings), then work ministries anyone can do—helps and governments—with tongues last. Paul the apostle still helped set up and clean up; good leaders work with the crew.

If any believing man or woman has widows, let them relieve them, and do not let the church be burdened, that it may relieve those who are really widows.

faqs.question: Should leaders just watch the crew work?
faqs.answer: No—a good leader works with the crew.

faqs.question: Were there three wise men?
faqs.answer: He says we don’t know how many—only that there were more than two.

faqs.question: Why did they choose seven deacons?
faqs.answer: Because that’s what they needed to get the job done.

faqs.question: Who is first responsible to help someone in need?
faqs.answer: The family; the church steps in for widows indeed with no family.

faqs.question: Why is the church important?
faqs.answer: Together we help grow people into mature Christians; keeping them saved is hard work.

faqs.question: What makes a good church?
faqs.answer: Good families, not eloquent preaching or numbers.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for raising children?
faqs.answer: Parents—not the government or help groups.

faqs.question: Do Christians work?
faqs.answer: Yes—everywhere he goes he says Christians work, because they value what God values.
